33793-the-seven-branched-candlestick-the.title: The Schooldays of Young American Jew
33793-the-seven-branched-candlestick-the.creator: Gilbert W. Gabriel
33793-the-seven-branched-candlestick-the.description: A book by Gilbert W. Gabriel. Born a Jew, I was not one. And this I can blame on no person excepting myself. Before my parents' death, they had urged me, pleaded with me to go to Sunday school at our reformed synagogue, to attend the Saturday morning services, to study the lore, that I might be confirmed into the religion of my fathers.

arxiv-1804-05508.title: Mass dependence of vector meson photoproduction off protons and nuclei within the energy-dependent hot-spot model Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-1804-05508.creator: J. Cepila, J. G. Contreras, M. Krelina, J. D. Tapia Takaki
arxiv-1804-05508.description: Abstract We study the photoproduction of vector mesons off proton and off nuclear targets. We work within the colour dipole model in an approach that includes subnucleon degrees of freedom, so-called hot spots, whose positions in the impact-parameter plane change event-by-event.

arxiv-1907-02147.title: Density of Inertial Particles: Exactly Solvable 2D Models
arxiv-1907-02147.creator: Leonid I. Piterbarg
arxiv-1907-02147.description: Abstract Abstract Inertial particles in 2D driven by a Gaussian white noise forcing are considered. For two examples of the forcing (compressible and incompressible) upper and lower bounds are found for the mean number of caustics as a function of Stokes number. Efficiency of the bounds is verified by numerical methods.

arxiv-2006-15667.title: Weak Signal Inclusion Under Sparsity and Dependence Thanks: Address for correspondence: X. Jessie Jeng, Department of Statistics, North Carolina State University, SAS Hall, 2311 Stinson Dr., Raleigh, NC 27695-8203, USA. E-mail: xjjeng@ncsu.edu.
arxiv-2006-15667.creator: X. Jessie Jeng, Yifei Hu
arxiv-2006-15667.description: Abstract We consider the scenario where important signals are not strong enough to be separable from a large amount of noise. Such weak signals commonly exist in large-scale data analysis and play vital roles in many biomedical applications. Existing methods however are mostly underpowered for such weak signals.

arxiv-2106-00291.title: Preview, Attend and Review: Schema-Aware Curriculum Learning for Multi-Domain Dialog State Tracking
arxiv-2106-00291.creator: Yinpei Dai, Hangyu Li, Yongbin Li, Jian Sun, Fei Huang, Luo Si, Xiaodan Zhu
arxiv-2106-00291.description: Abstract Existing dialog state tracking (DST) models are trained with dialog data in a random order, neglecting rich structural information in a dataset. In this paper, we propose to use curriculum learning (CL) to better leverage both the curriculum structure and schema structure for task-oriented dialogs.

arxiv-2106-13512.title: The L2L System for Second Language Learning Using Visualised Zoom Calls Among Students Thanks: The research was partly supported by Science Foundation Ireland under Grant Number SFI/12/RC/2289_P2, co-funded by the European Regional Development Fund. Affiliation: School of Applied Languages and Inter
arxiv-2106-13512.creator: Aparajita Dey-Plissonneau 1, Hyowon Lee 2, Vincent Pradier 3, Michael Scriney 2, Alan F. Smeaton 2
arxiv-2106-13512.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Aparajita Dey-Plissonneau 1, Hyowon Lee 2, Vincent Pradier 3, Michael Scriney 2, Alan F. Smeaton 2. An important part of second language learning is conversation which is best practised with speakers whose native language is the language being learned. We facilitate this by pairing students from different countries learning each others’ native language. Mixed groups of students have Zoom calls, half in one language and half in the other, in order to practice and improve their conversation skills.

arxiv-2202-05758.title: Using Random Perturbations to Mitigate Adversarial Attacks on Sentiment Analysis Models
arxiv-2202-05758.creator: Abigail Swenor, Jugal Kalita
arxiv-2202-05758.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Abigail Swenor, Jugal Kalita. Attacks on deep learning models are often difficult to identify and therefore are difficult to protect against. This problem is exacerbated by the use of public datasets that typically are not manually inspected before use. In this paper, we offer a solution to this vulnerability by using, during testing, random perturbations such as spelling correction if necessary, substitution by random synonym, or simply dropping the word.

arxiv-2202-06214.title: On equivariant Lie-Yamaguti algebras and related structures
arxiv-2202-06214.creator: Shuangjian Guo, Bibhash Mondal, Ripan Saha 1. School of Mathematics and Statistics, Guizhou University of Finance and EconomicsGuiyang 550025, P. R. of China2. Department of Mathematics, Behala CollegeBehala 700060, Kolkata, India3. Department of Mathematics, Raiganj UniversityRaiganj 733134, West B
arxiv-2202-06214.description: Abstract ABSTRACT In this paper, we first discuss cohomology and a one-parameter formal deformation theory of Lie-Yamaguti algebras. Next, we study finite group actions on Lie-Yamaguti algebras and introduce equivariant cohomology for Lie-Yamaguti algebras equipped with group actions. Finally, we study an equivariant one-parameter formal deformation theory and show that our equivariant cohomology is the suitable deformation cohomology.

arxiv-2409-17572.title: Dr. GPT in Campus Counseling: Understanding Higher Education Students’ Opinions on LLM-assisted Mental Health Services DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in HCI CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in collaborative and social
arxiv-2409-17572.creator: Owen Xingjian Zhang, Shuyao Zhou, Jiayi Geng, Yuhan Liu, Sunny Xun Liu
arxiv-2409-17572.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Owen Xingjian Zhang, Shuyao Zhou, Jiayi Geng, Yuhan Liu, Sunny Xun Liu. In response to the increasing mental health challenges faced by college students, we sought to understand their perspectives on how AI applications, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), can be leveraged to enhance their mental well-being. Through pilot interviews with ten diverse students, we explored their opinions on the use of LLMs across five fictional scenarios: General Information Inquiry, Initial Screening, Reshaping Patient-Expert Dynamics, Long-term Care, and Follow-up Care.

pmc-10566589.creator: Jessica Mannette, Yingying Zhang, Melissa Rothfus, Chelsey Purdy, Winta Tesfatsion, Mary Lynch, Barbara Hamilton-Hinch, Patricia L Williams, Phillip Joy, Shannan Grant
pmc-10566589.description: Objective:The objective of this scoping review was to map the current literature and resources available on nutrition and food programming for people living with HIV in Canada. This review is phase 1 of a 4-phase project, called FoodNOW (Food to eNhance Our Wellness), a community-based nutritional needs assessment of people living with HIV in Nova Scotia, Canada.

pmc-11455109.title: 6983 Pembrolizimab Induced Hypophysitis: Uncommon Side Effect Leading To Late Diagnosis
pmc-11455109.creator: Taibah Chaudhary, Omar Syed, Archana Shridar, Ravleen Kaur, Omaima Chaudhary, Muhammad Saad Zubair
pmc-11455109.description: Disclosure: T. Chaudhary: None. O. Syed: None. A. Shridar: None. R. Kaur: None. O. Chaudhary: None. M.S. Zubair: None. Background: Pembrolizumab, an immune checkpoint inhibitor, has shown efficacy inducing remission in various malignancies. Associated immune-related adverse effects (irAEs) have been recorded but cases of concomitant hypophysitis and thyroiditis are rare.

pmc-13029845.title: A 94 GHz Millimeter-Wave Radar System for Remote Vehicle Height Measurement to Prevent Bridge Collisions
pmc-13029845.creator: Natan Steinmetz, Eyal Magori, Yael Balal, Yonatan B. Sudai, Nezah Balal
pmc-13029845.description: Collisions between over-height vehicles and low-clearance bridges cause infrastructure damage and pose safety risks. Existing detection systems rely primarily on optical sensors, which suffer from performance degradation in adverse weather conditions. This paper presents an alternative approach based on a 94 GHz millimeter-wave radar that achieves velocity-independent height measurement.

pmc-13079970.title: Shift current anomalous photovoltaics in a double perovskite ferroelectric
pmc-13079970.creator: Linjie Wei, Fu Li, Yi Liu, Hongbin Zhang, Junhua Luo, Zhihua Sun
pmc-13079970.description: SignificanceFerroelectric anomalous photovoltaic (APV) effect holds a great promise in the new optoelectronic application fields. Nevertheless, the limited understanding of ferroelectric APV effect mechanism hinders the exploration of new APV-active candidates. Recently, the shift current model exhibits unique insights into the bulk photovoltaic effect and has attracted considerable attention.

pmc-13226125.description: Prime editing is a versatile gene editing technology that has undergone significant enhancements since its inception. Currently, a recently reported prime editing system, PE7 combined with MLH1dn, incorporates two auxiliary components designed to enhance editing efficiency: La fused to the reverse transcriptase (RT) and non-recruited MLH1dn.

pmc-13326661.title: Petromaroside A, an unprecedented natural nucleoside from the sponge Petrosia sp. with potent cytotoxicity and biosynthetic insight
pmc-13326661.creator: Phuong Vu Luu, Huong Lien Ton-Nu, Hien Minh Nguyen, Cuong-Quoc Nguyen, Quang Minh Thai, Kuei-Hung Lai
pmc-13326661.description: A chemical investigation of the marine sponge Petrosia sp. led to the isolation of a novel nucleoside, petromaroside A (1), featuring an unprecedented C-5′ hydroxymethylated deoxyribose moiety, along with thymidine (2). These structures and their absolute configurations were elucidated by comprehensive spectroscopic analyses and quantum chemical calculations, including NMR, HRESIMS, LC-MS/MS, GIAO-NMR calculations, and DP4+ probability analysis.

pmc-13477293.creator: Yusheng Zhou, Jonathan Houle, Valeria Raparelli, Colleen M Norris, Louise Pilote
